provenance.note: git_head is HEAD at generation time (the parent of the commit containing these results); source_dirty covers src/, run_experiments.py, pyproject.toml and tests/ only

design.scope: Numerical equivalence and coordinate contracts for the additive Gaussian layer; not a performance or fault-classification benchmark.
design.tolerance_units: Original kg for means, kg^2 for covariance entries, dimensionless for NIS; fixed before running.
design.noise: Independent process and observation noise across times and from the initial error; full correlated R retained. Q is conserving random exchange.
design.reference: Independent direct-solve ordinary affine KF with Joseph covariance; receives observations and masks, never physical truth or fault labels.
design.pairing: The same eight noise seeds are reused across scenarios and charts. These are paired numerical comparisons, not independent performance trials.
design.order: Predict, then assimilate each sample jointly using the observed principal R submatrix. Sensor permutation/scaling preserves its mask and correlations.
design.chart_interpretation: Fixed affine coordinate changes x'=T x+c, not physical interventions. Translation changes the coordinate origin, not an automorphism of the zero-identity additive group; centered errors transform as T e.
design.statistic: NIS is the pre-update innovation Mahalanobis statistic. Update/no_observations statuses are processing outcomes, not fault verdicts. No alarm threshold is used.
design.limits: The additive layer equals ordinary KF for this affine Gaussian model. No nonlinear IEKF accuracy, robustness, calibration or sensor-identification gain is claimed. Coordinate changes cannot resolve existing fault ambiguity.
